name: K'iche', Joyabaj
confidence_why: 3 independent first-hand sources agree (1 agree, 1 refine), none contradicts

audit.action: check whether this is the same language as another entry
audit.recode_to: If the dialect record is kept: final stress (final primary, no secondary marks), kind aligned with parent kich1262, grade 'inherited from kich1262 (Henderson 2012, non-Joyabaj data)'. Preferably fold kich1263-1267 into kich1262: six records, one quotation, zero dialect-specific sources.
audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: (1) Quotation verified verbatim in the cited Henderson 2012 preprint p. 26 ex. (82) (file now saved in our check folder); Bennett 2016:495 corroboration verified. (2) The source is a 2012 phonology article with fieldwork on Santa Cruz del Quiché / Santa Lucía Utatlán K'ichee' (fn. 1), applied to the Joyabaj dialect languoid, which exists in the catalog only because of the retired ISO code [quj]; Glottolog lists 0 descriptive refs for kich1267 and no Joyabaj stress description was found on the web (SIL has only Doty & Souder 1971 folk texts). (3) The record's rule encodes iambic secondary stresses that come from our earlier survey Wikipedia hint, not from Henderson — Henderson p. 27 rejects iambic footing and Bennett 2016:497 calls Mayan secondary-stress reports impressionistic — and the parent record kich1262 codes the same quotation as fixed-strict without secondaries, so the family of six

sources.quote: "K'ICHEE' STRESS GENERALIZATION: Stress falls on the final syllable of a prosodic word, unless that syllable is light non-root material, in which case it falls on the final root syllable." (Henderson 2012, preprint p. 26, ex. (82); "The first part of the generalization is that stress is attracted to the right edge of the prosodic word." (same page). sources.quote: 'Primary stress is word-final in non-verbs in Chichicastenango K'iche', with the exclusion of two extrametrical suffixes' ... 'In verbs, stress is sensitive to vowel quality and syllable shape. Stress falls on the left-most syllable containing either a tense vowel or a coda, or if there are none, on the final syllable.' Describes the neighbouring eastern variety (kich1265), not Joyabaj; shows eastern K'iche' dialects can depart from plain final stress.
